title: Fewest Domino Rotations
statement:
A row of dominoes is given by two lists: `tops[i]` is the number on the top half of domino `i` and `bottoms[i]` the number on its bottom half (numbers 1 to 6). A **rotation** turns one domino around, swapping its top and bottom.

Return the **fewest rotations** after which **all the top numbers are equal** or **all the bottom numbers are equal**, or `-1` if that is impossible. For an empty row the answer is `0`.

examples.explanation: Rotate the second domino: the tops become 3, 3, 3, 3.
No number appears on every domino.

hints.nudge: If every top (or every bottom) is to become the same number x, then x must be on every domino. Which numbers can x possibly be, looking only at the first domino?
hints.pattern: Only the two numbers of the first domino are candidates. For each candidate count the dominoes where it is missing from the top and from the bottom; the cost is the smaller of the two counts, and it is impossible if some domino has neither side equal to the candidate.
hints.walkthrough: You could try every number 1 to 6 as the target (six passes), but the first domino already limits the choice: the target must appear on it, so it is tops[0] or bottoms[0]. For a target x, every domino must show x on at least one side, otherwise the target is impossible. To get x on the TOP you rotate exactly the dominoes that have x only on the bottom; to get x on the BOTTOM you rotate those that have x only on the top. A domino with x on both sides never needs rotating. Take the cheaper of the two goals, then the cheaper of the two candidates; if both candidates are impossible, return -1. One pass per candidate.
